@netdpb This is the last contentious part of the review. 

Can you take a peak here and let me know if you have thoughts on how we can remove this check? I've added a stacktrace that details what blows up when the check is removed.

First off, the lambda doesn't appear to use its parameter, `contributionBinding`.

Second, if `parentBindings` is truly the `ResolvedBindings` that was previously resolved in the parent component, how could its owning component be this subcomponent?

I guess because `dependsOnLocalBindings` searches through the dependencies, and `getPreviouslyResolvedBindings` may in fact return bindings previously resolved in this very component, they might be. So calling the parameter "parentBindings" is actually wrong.

-----

I have to say I'm becoming more and more convinced that the whole strategy this `LocalDependencyChecker` uses is fundamentally broken. We use it for two things:

1. Determining whether we can skip resolving a binding key in this component because it was already resolved in the parent and there's nothing local to conflict.
2. Determining which component owns a binding after it was resolved.

The work done for (1) means that we're effectively resolving the binding in order to figure out whether we should skip resolving the binding, which is self-defeating. And the work done for (2) effectively repeats the resolution after resolving every binding.

I think we should stop doing (1) at all, and take a different approach to (2). For (2), currently we create a `ResolvedBindings`, figuring out which component owns each contained binding using the `LocalDependencyChecker`, and then we resolve its direct dependencies. How about instead we resolve like this:

1. Look up the bindings without checking ownership.
2. For each binding:
   1. Find its owning resolver (`getOwningResolver`).
   2. Resolve its direct dependencies (recursive call to `resolve`).
   3. The binding's owning component is whichever is the lowest (farthest from the root) among the owning resolver's component and all of the direct dependencies' owning components.

That way, each binding that has ANY transitive dependencies in the current component, conflicting or not, is copied down to the current component even if it is also owned in an ancestor.

I think changing to this approach will make resolution more performant and less buggy.

-----

It'll probably take a fair amount of experimentation and refactoring and discussion, and I don't know how much time you have to spend on this. Let me know how you want to proceed; if you don't feel like this is something you can commit to right now, we'll definitely work on this ourselves soon.

In either case, let me say that without your work here, and #629 filed by @guliash, I don't think we'd understand the problems with `LocalDependencyChecker` nearly as well, so thank you.
